subject: FRE
label: Grade 07
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 07 French, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Describing my town
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Describing my town', you learn to describe a town. You work with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Describing my town' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: describe a town, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: 'Mon ecole est grande. J'ai un cartable et une trousse. J'etudie les maths et l'anglais.' Swap in your own words. Method: Model run for 'Describing my town'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Describe a town: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Describe the town in general. Ma ville est petite et calme. [My town is small and quiet.] Elle est au bord de la mer. [It is by the sea.] Il y a une place, un marché, un parc et une gare. [There is a square, a market, a park and a station.]

Step 2, Say where things are with prepositions. Le marché est en face de la mairie. [The market is opposite the town hall.] Le parc est à côté de l'école. [The park is next to the school.] La gare est près du centre mais loin de la plage. [The station is near the centre but far from the beach.]

Step 3, Give directions. Pour aller à la gare, allez tout droit. [To go to the station, go straight on.] Tournez à gauche, puis à droite. [Turn left, then right.] C'est à cinq minutes à pied. [It is five minutes on foot.] Use the vous form to be polite.

Step 4, Dialogue with a visitor. Touriste : Excusez-moi, où est la mairie ? [Excuse me, where is the town hall?] Vous : Elle est en face du marché. [It is opposite the market.] Touriste : Merci beaucoup ! [Thank you very much!] Vous : De rien. [You are welcome.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says à côté la gare. Correction: à côté de la gare. Another says Il y a beaucoup des magasins. Correction: Il y a beaucoup de magasins. Also de + le becomes du: près du parc, not près de le parc.

Step 6, Your turn: describe your town with two places and one direction. Model answer: Ma ville est animée. Il y a un marché en face de la gare. Pour aller à l'école, tournez à droite. [My town is lively. There is a market opposite the station. To go to school, turn right.]

modules.title: Adjective agreement and cause
modules.outcome: use adjective agreement and express cause
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Adjective agreement and cause', you learn to use adjective agreement and express cause. You work with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Adjective agreement and cause' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: use adjective agreement and express cause, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: un petit chat, une petite chatte. Plural: add -s (les chats noirs). Feminine usually adds -e. Method: Model run for 'Adjective agreement and cause'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Use adjective agreement and express cause: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Adjectives agree with the noun. grand, grande, grands, grandes [tall or big]. Le parc est grand. La place est grande. Les parcs sont grands. Les places sont grandes. Add e for feminine and s for plural.

Step 2, Learn an irregular adjective. beau [beautiful, masculine], belle [feminine], beaux [masculine plural], belles [feminine plural]. Un beau jardin. Une belle maison. De beaux arbres. De belles fleurs. Say each phrase aloud.

Step 3, Express cause with parce que. J'aime ma ville parce qu'elle est calme. [I like my town because it is quiet.] Before a vowel, que becomes qu'. Also use car [for, because]: Je reste ici, car j'aime la mer. [I stay here, as I love the sea.]

Step 4, Use à cause de with a noun. Nous restons à la maison à cause de la pluie. [We stay at home because of the rain.] Combine: Les rues sont belles parce que les habitants plantent des fleurs. [The streets are beautiful because the inhabitants plant flowers.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says Les maisons sont beau. Correction: Les maisons sont belles. Another says à cause que. Correction: parce que before a clause, à cause de before a noun. A third says parce que elle; use parce qu'elle.

Step 6, Your turn: write one sentence about the beautiful gardens and one with because of the wind. Model answer: Les jardins sont beaux parce que les gens les aiment. Nous ne sortons pas à cause du vent. [The gardens are beautiful because people love them. We do not go out because of the wind.]

modules.title: Reading comprehension
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Reading comprehension', you learn to answer in full. You work with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. You see it, say it, then do it alone.

Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Texte: 'Lea habite a Lyon. Elle a douze ans. Elle aime lire.' Ou habite Lea? A Lyon. A toi d'ecrire: 'Je m'appelle... J'habite a... J'aime...' Method: Model run for 'Reading comprehension'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Answer in full: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Read the text once, then again. Hier, Clara est allée à la piscine avec sa cousine. Elles ont nagé pendant une heure, puis elles ont mangé une glace. Clara n'a pas pris son bonnet, alors le maître nageur lui a prêté un bonnet. [Yesterday Clara went to the pool with her cousin. They swam for an hour, then ate an ice cream. Clara did not take her cap, so the lifeguard lent her one.]

Step 2, Spot the tense and the helper verb. Aller uses être: Clara est allée. Nager and manger use avoir: elles ont nagé, elles ont mangé. These are the passé composé, for finished past actions. Underline each helper verb and its past participle before you answer.

Step 3, Turn the question into the start of your answer. Où est allée Clara ? becomes Clara est allée à la piscine. Qu'est-ce qu'elles ont mangé ? becomes Elles ont mangé une glace. Reuse the same helper verb and past participle as the question.

Step 4, Give reasons in full. Pourquoi le maître nageur a-t-il prêté un bonnet à Clara ? [Why did the lifeguard lend Clara a cap?] Answer in a full sentence: Le maître nageur a prêté un bonnet à Clara parce qu'elle n'a pas pris le sien. Do not answer with only Parce que.

Step 5, Fix errors. A child writes Clara est allé. Correction: allée, because être verbs agree with the subject and Clara is feminine. Another writes Elles ont allé. Correction: Elles sont allées. Another writes Clara a pas pris. Correction: Clara n'a pas pris, with ne and pas around a.
Step 6, Your turn: answer Combien de temps ont-elles nagé ? [How long did they swim?] Answer: Elles ont nagé pendant une heure. [They swam for an hour.]

modules.standard: Write a short text: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Plan a short letter in four parts: greeting, about me, last weekend, a question. Open with Chère Zoé, for a girl or Cher Zoé, for a boy. Close with À bientôt or Amitiés. Write the plan as four bullets before you start the full text.

Step 2, Write the opening and the present tense. Chère Zoé, merci pour ta lettre. Je m'appelle Ibrahim et j'ai douze ans. J'habite dans un appartement près d'un parc. [Dear Zoé, thank you for your letter. My name is Ibrahim and I am twelve. I live in a flat near a park.]

Step 3, Add the past with the passé composé. Le week-end dernier, j'ai joué au basket et j'ai visité un musée avec mon père. [Last weekend I played basketball and visited a museum with my father.] Both verbs use avoir plus the past participle: joué, visité.

Step 4, Close with a question and a sign-off. Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu aimes faire ? Écris-moi vite ! [And you, what do you like to do? Write to me soon!] Amitiés, Ibrahim. Count about 55 words. Read the letter aloud and check each verb.

Step 5, Fix errors. A child writes J'ai allé au musée. Correction: Je suis allé au musée, because aller takes être. Another writes Cher Zoé to a girl. Correction: Chère Zoé. A third writes j'ai joue. Correction: j'ai joué, with the é ending.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences about last weekend using the passé composé. Model answer: Samedi dernier, j'ai regardé un film. Dimanche, je suis allée chez ma grand-mère. J'ai mangé un bon gâteau. [Last Saturday I watched a film. On Sunday I went to my grandmother's. I ate a good cake.]

ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
